name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2025, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 7,400 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/jan2025_contributionandallocationrates.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year . An incomplete registration does not waive the statutory or fund contribution for an otherwise covered worker; assess the declared liability and retain the registration warning. CPF Act First Schedule para 2 — the December AW ceiling is charged against every AW of the year, an opening (prior-system) AW included; the year's AW paid is read as at least the AW already charged to date (`scheme.year_to_date.base − .ordinary`). Ceiling: an opening AW plus earlier payslip AW in one year still undercounts; the full fix is an opening-AW context field.

name: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund
authority: CPF Board self-help group contribution schedule: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund. Monthly employee-borne wage-band deductions apply to every employee of the Indian community, whatever the residency or pass: CPF Act 1953 s.76(3) requires the deduction from “an employee who belongs to that community”, s.2 “employee” is any person employed in Singapore, and SINDA Rules 1992 r.2 (unlike CDAC Rules r.2, which confines the Chinese community to citizens and permanent residents) sets no residency condition. The CPF Board’s narrower list (citizens, SPRs, Employment Pass holders) is guidance the Rules do not carry. A dual election records SINDA as a second fund for an employee of Indian descent whose first NRIC race selects another fund. The Indian community is the one CPF (Contributions to Community Fund — SINDA) Rules 1992 r.2 defines: “every person of Indian descent and includes Bangladeshis, Bengalis, Gujaratis, Parsees, Sikhs, Sinhalese, Telegus, Pakistanis, Sri Lankans, Goanese, Malayalees, Punjabis, Sindhis and Tamils” (read on sso.agc.gov.sg, current version as at 28 Sep 2026), so each of those NRIC races is read as SINDA’s, not only INDIAN. NRIC races are read in the spelling of the ICA-sourced Myinfo RaceCode list (Myinfo API code tables, public.cloud.myinfo.gov.sg, v1.11, read 2026-09-28): TELUGU and GOAN beside the Rules' Telegus and Goanese; CEYLONESE and CEYLON MOOR as Sri Lankans; and, by the Rules' "every person of Indian descent", OTHER INDIAN, MALABARI, MARATHI, MAHRATTA, HINDUSTANI, BRAHMIN, RAJPUT, ASSAMI, MANIPURI and KHASI (peoples whose origin lies wholly within India, Pakistan, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka). A single mixed-descent code goes to the fund of its first-named descent (the Board's first-race rule), so SINO INDIAN is CDAC's and ANGLO INDIAN ECF's, and a dual election adds SINDA; codes of wider origin (NEPALESE, GURKHA, BHUTANESE, MALDIVIAN, PATHAN, NAGA, AFGHAN) are not read as SINDA's. The base includes cash wage allowances, overtime and leave encashment, less unpaid absence; official expense reimbursements are excluded. The published wage band applies unless a dated fund instruction records an opt-out or a different monthly amount. Explicit zero is distinct from no instruction. The instruction reference is required; MBMF changes use the approved total after any component changes. CPF Board: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups . SINDA instructions remain valid only with the same employer: https://www.sinda.org.sg/donate/sindafundcontribution/ . An incomplete registration does not waive the statutory or fund contribution for an otherwise covered worker; assess the declared liability and retain the registration warning. Owner rule 2026-09-29: the CPF Board list is guidance the Rules do not carry, so the Rules govern — an S Pass, Work Permit or unclassified foreign-pass holder of the Indian community is deducted under r.2 on the same wage bands as any other employee of that community, and the earlier refusal of that class is withdrawn.

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–4 and Skills Development Levy (Exemption) Order 2014 para.2(1)(a): a matriculated or registered student of one of twelve named local institutions employed for institution-approved training is exempt. Other student paths are not inferred from an internship label. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–3: levy applies to an employee serving wholly or partly in Singapore during the month, or on leave attributable to earlier Singapore service; it excludes a domestic servant, gardener or chauffeur wholly and exclusively employed by an individual outside that individual’s trade, business, profession or vocation. The employer owes 0.25% of monthly money wages, minimum SGD 2 and maximum SGD 11.25. The local tertiary student exemption is priced from declared standing and institution approval; the overseas-tertiary and school-holiday classes remain separately under review. The CPF Board rounds the employer-month total for local employees, paid with CPF, down to the nearest dollar; the levy for foreign employees is submitted at the actual amount (SkillsFuture Singapore FAQs on the October 2023 SDL Notice of Assessment, F.7, https://file.go.gov.sg/sdl-noa2023faqs.pdf, kept as historical evidence of the practice). Since 1 July 2026 the Agency is the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) (SDL Act s.2 as amended by Act 17 of 2026), and the CPF Board collects SDL on its behalf. Sources: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/SDLA1979?ProvIds=pr2-,pr3- ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy .

name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year . An incomplete registration does not waive the statutory or fund contribution for an otherwise covered worker; assess the declared liability and retain the registration warning. CPF Act First Schedule para 2 — the December AW ceiling is charged against every AW of the year, an opening (prior-system) AW included; the year's AW paid is read as at least the AW already charged to date (`scheme.year_to_date.base − .ordinary`). Ceiling: an opening AW plus earlier payslip AW in one year still undercounts; the full fix is an opening-AW context field.

name: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund
authority: CPF Board self-help group contribution schedule: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund. Monthly employee-borne wage-band deductions apply to every employee of the Indian community, whatever the residency or pass: CPF Act 1953 s.76(3) requires the deduction from “an employee who belongs to that community”, s.2 “employee” is any person employed in Singapore, and SINDA Rules 1992 r.2 (unlike CDAC Rules r.2, which confines the Chinese community to citizens and permanent residents) sets no residency condition. The CPF Board’s narrower list (citizens, SPRs, Employment Pass holders) is guidance the Rules do not carry. A dual election records SINDA as a second fund for an employee of Indian descent whose first NRIC race selects another fund. The Indian community is the one CPF (Contributions to Community Fund — SINDA) Rules 1992 r.2 defines: “every person of Indian descent and includes Bangladeshis, Bengalis, Gujaratis, Parsees, Sikhs, Sinhalese, Telegus, Pakistanis, Sri Lankans, Goanese, Malayalees, Punjabis, Sindhis and Tamils” (read on sso.agc.gov.sg, current version as at 28 Sep 2026), so each of those NRIC races is read as SINDA’s, not only INDIAN. NRIC races are read in the spelling of the ICA-sourced Myinfo RaceCode list (Myinfo API code tables, public.cloud.myinfo.gov.sg, v1.11, read 2026-09-28): TELUGU and GOAN beside the Rules' Telegus and Goanese; CEYLONESE and CEYLON MOOR as Sri Lankans; and, by the Rules' "every person of Indian descent", OTHER INDIAN, MALABARI, MARATHI, MAHRATTA, HINDUSTANI, BRAHMIN, RAJPUT, ASSAMI, MANIPURI and KHASI (peoples whose origin lies wholly within India, Pakistan, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka). A single mixed-descent code goes to the fund of its first-named descent (the Board's first-race rule), so SINO INDIAN is CDAC's and ANGLO INDIAN ECF's, and a dual election adds SINDA; codes of wider origin (NEPALESE, GURKHA, BHUTANESE, MALDIVIAN, PATHAN, NAGA, AFGHAN) are not read as SINDA's. The base includes cash wage allowances, overtime and leave encashment, less unpaid absence; official expense reimbursements are excluded. The published wage band applies unless a dated fund instruction records an opt-out or a different monthly amount. Explicit zero is distinct from no instruction. The instruction reference is required; MBMF changes use the approved total after any component changes. CPF Board: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups . SINDA instructions remain valid only with the same employer: https://www.sinda.org.sg/donate/sindafundcontribution/ . An incomplete registration does not waive the statutory or fund contribution for an otherwise covered worker; assess the declared liability and retain the registration warning. Owner rule 2026-09-29: the CPF Board list is guidance the Rules do not carry, so the Rules govern — an S Pass, Work Permit or unclassified foreign-pass holder of the Indian community is deducted under r.2 on the same wage bands as any other employee of that community, and the earlier refusal of that class is withdrawn.

name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–4 and Skills Development Levy (Exemption) Order 2014 para.2(1)(a): a matriculated or registered student of one of twelve named local institutions employed for institution-approved training is exempt. Other student paths are not inferred from an internship label. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–3: levy applies to an employee serving wholly or partly in Singapore during the month, or on leave attributable to earlier Singapore service; it excludes a domestic servant, gardener or chauffeur wholly and exclusively employed by an individual outside that individual’s trade, business, profession or vocation. The local tertiary student exemption is priced from declared standing and institution approval; the overseas-tertiary and school-holiday classes remain separately under review. Since 1 July 2026 the Agency is the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) (SDL Act s.2 as amended by Act 17 of 2026), and the CPF Board collects SDL on its behalf. name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2026, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. An incomplete registration does not waive the statutory or fund contribution for an otherwise covered worker; assess the declared liability and retain the registration warning. name: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund
authority: CPF Board self-help group contribution schedule: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund. Monthly employee-borne wage-band deductions apply to every employee of the Indian community, whatever the residency or pass: CPF Act 1953 s.76(3) requires the deduction from “an employee who belongs to that community”, s.2 “employee” is any person employed in Singapore, and SINDA Rules 1992 r.2 (unlike CDAC Rules r.2, which confines the Chinese community to citizens and permanent residents) sets no residency condition. The CPF Board’s narrower list (citizens, SPRs, Employment Pass holders) is guidance the Rules do not carry. A dual election records SINDA as a second fund for an employee of Indian descent whose first NRIC race selects another fund. The Indian community is the one CPF (Contributions to Community Fund — SINDA) Rules 1992 r.2 defines: “every person of Indian descent and includes Bangladeshis, Bengalis, Gujaratis, Parsees, Sikhs, Sinhalese, Telegus, Pakistanis, Sri Lankans, Goanese, Malayalees, Punjabis, Sindhis and Tamils” (read on sso.agc.gov.sg, current version as at 28 Sep 2026), so each of those NRIC races is read as SINDA’s, not only INDIAN. NRIC races are read in the spelling of the ICA-sourced Myinfo RaceCode list (Myinfo API code tables, public.cloud.myinfo.gov.sg, v1.11, read 2026-09-28): TELUGU and GOAN beside the Rules' Telegus and Goanese; CEYLONESE and CEYLON MOOR as Sri Lankans; and, by the Rules' "every person of Indian descent", OTHER INDIAN, MALABARI, MARATHI, MAHRATTA, HINDUSTANI, BRAHMIN, RAJPUT, ASSAMI, MANIPURI and KHASI (peoples whose origin lies wholly within India, Pakistan, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka). A single mixed-descent code goes to the fund of its first-named descent (the Board's first-race rule), so SINO INDIAN is CDAC's and ANGLO INDIAN ECF's, and a dual election adds SINDA; codes of wider origin (NEPALESE, GURKHA, BHUTANESE, MALDIVIAN, PATHAN, NAGA, AFGHAN) are not read as SINDA's. The base includes cash wage allowances, overtime and leave encashment, less unpaid absence; official expense reimbursements are excluded. The published wage band applies unless a dated fund instruction records an opt-out or a different monthly amount. Explicit zero is distinct from no instruction. The instruction reference is required; MBMF changes use the approved total after any component changes. CPF Board: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups . name: Central Provident Fund
authority: Central Provident Fund Act 1953, section 7 and First Schedule; CPF Board contribution tables effective 1 January 2027, Tables 1–5. Ordinary Wages are capped at SGD 8,000 per month. Additional Wages, including bonuses and leave encashment, use the SGD 102,000 annual ceiling less the year's capped Ordinary Wages. Before year end, remaining Ordinary Wages are projected; year-end and departure calculations reconcile against actual wages. Cash wage allowances enter their declared Ordinary or Additional Wage part; official expense reimbursements do not. Rate bands change in the month after the relevant birthday. SPR year two starts in the month after the first anniversary; year three starts in the month after the second anniversary. First- and second-year SPRs use graduated rates unless CPF Board approves full employer/full employee or full employer/graduated employee rates. These are separate elections with an approval reference. The total contribution rounds half-up to whole dollars, the employee share rounds down, and the employer pays the difference. Published tables: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf . CPF Board: the AW ceiling is per employee, employer and calendar year; related-company transfer may share one ceiling only under Board approval and stated conditions. https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/how-do-i-apply-the-additional-wage-ceiling-for-the-following-scenarios-a-employee-a-is-working-for-two-companies-concurrently-b-employee-b-is-transferred-from-another-entity ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/as-an-employer-how-do-i-apply-to-the-board-for-a-single-additional-wage-aw-ceiling-if-my-employees-were-transferred-to-another-related-company-during-the-year . An incomplete registration does not waive the statutory or fund contribution for an otherwise covered worker; assess the declared liability and retain the registration warning. CPF Act First Schedule para 2 — the December AW ceiling is charged against every AW of the year, an opening (prior-system) AW included; the year's AW paid is read as at least the AW already charged to date (`scheme.year_to_date.base − .ordinary`). Ceiling: an opening AW plus earlier payslip AW in one year still undercounts; the full fix is an opening-AW context field.

name: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund
authority: CPF Board self-help group contribution schedule: Singapore Indian Development Association Fund. Monthly employee-borne wage-band deductions apply to every employee of the Indian community, whatever the residency or pass: CPF Act 1953 s.76(3) requires the deduction from “an employee who belongs to that community”, s.2 “employee” is any person employed in Singapore, and SINDA Rules 1992 r.2 (unlike CDAC Rules r.2, which confines the Chinese community to citizens and permanent residents) sets no residency condition. The CPF Board’s narrower list (citizens, SPRs, Employment Pass holders) is guidance the Rules do not carry. A dual election records SINDA as a second fund for an employee of Indian descent whose first NRIC race selects another fund. The Indian community is the one CPF (Contributions to Community Fund — SINDA) Rules 1992 r.2 defines: “every person of Indian descent and includes Bangladeshis, Bengalis, Gujaratis, Parsees, Sikhs, Sinhalese, Telegus, Pakistanis, Sri Lankans, Goanese, Malayalees, Punjabis, Sindhis and Tamils” (read on sso.agc.gov.sg, current version as at 28 Sep 2026), so each of those NRIC races is read as SINDA’s, not only INDIAN. NRIC races are read in the spelling of the ICA-sourced Myinfo RaceCode list (Myinfo API code tables, public.cloud.myinfo.gov.sg, v1.11, read 2026-09-28): TELUGU and GOAN beside the Rules' Telegus and Goanese; CEYLONESE and CEYLON MOOR as Sri Lankans; and, by the Rules' "every person of Indian descent", OTHER INDIAN, MALABARI, MARATHI, MAHRATTA, HINDUSTANI, BRAHMIN, RAJPUT, ASSAMI, MANIPURI and KHASI (peoples whose origin lies wholly within India, Pakistan, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka). A single mixed-descent code goes to the fund of its first-named descent (the Board's first-race rule), so SINO INDIAN is CDAC's and ANGLO INDIAN ECF's, and a dual election adds SINDA; codes of wider origin (NEPALESE, GURKHA, BHUTANESE, MALDIVIAN, PATHAN, NAGA, AFGHAN) are not read as SINDA's. The base includes cash wage allowances, overtime and leave encashment, less unpaid absence; official expense reimbursements are excluded. The published wage band applies unless a dated fund instruction records an opt-out or a different monthly amount. Explicit zero is distinct from no instruction. The instruction reference is required; MBMF changes use the approved total after any component changes. CPF Board: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/contributions-to-self-help-groups . name: Skills Development Levy
authority: Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–4 and Skills Development Levy (Exemption) Order 2014 para.2(1)(a): a matriculated or registered student of one of twelve named local institutions employed for institution-approved training is exempt. Other student paths are not inferred from an internship label. Skills Development Levy Act 1979 ss.2–3: levy applies to an employee serving wholly or partly in Singapore during the month, or on leave attributable to earlier Singapore service; it excludes a domestic servant, gardener or chauffeur wholly and exclusively employed by an individual outside that individual’s trade, business, profession or vocation. The employer owes 0.25% of monthly money wages, minimum SGD 2 and maximum SGD 11.25. The local tertiary student exemption is priced from declared standing and institution approval; the overseas-tertiary and school-holiday classes remain separately under review. The CPF Board rounds the employer-month total for local employees, paid with CPF, down to the nearest dollar; the levy for foreign employees is submitted at the actual amount (SkillsFuture Singapore FAQs on the October 2023 SDL Notice of Assessment, F.7, https://file.go.gov.sg/sdl-noa2023faqs.pdf, kept as historical evidence of the practice). Since 1 July 2026 the Agency is the Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA) (SDL Act s.2 as amended by Act 17 of 2026), and the CPF Board collects SDL on its behalf. Sources: https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/SDLA1979?ProvIds=pr2-,pr3- ; https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/employer-obligations/skills-development-levy .
